arxiv-2109-03755.title: Feature Selection on Thermal-stress Dataset
arxiv-2109-03755.creator: Xuyang Shen, Jo Plested, Tom Gedeon
arxiv-2109-03755.description: Abstract Physical symptoms caused by high stress commonly happen in our daily lives, leading to the importance of stress recognition systems. This study aims to improve stress classification by selecting appropriate features from Thermal-stress data, ANUstressDB. We explored three different feature selection techniques: correlation analysis, magnitude measure, and genetic algorithm.

arxiv-2306-12165.title: Post-hoc Selection of Pareto-Optimal Solutions in Search and Recommendation Conference: xxx; xxx; xxx Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2306-12165.creator: Vincenzo Paparella, Vito Walter Anelli, Franco Maria Nardini, Raffaele Perego, Tommaso Di Noia
arxiv-2306-12165.description: Abstract . Information Retrieval (IR) and Recommender Systems (RS) tasks are moving from computing a ranking of final results based on a single metric to multi-objective problems. Solving these problems leads to a set of Pareto-optimal solutions, known as Pareto frontier, in which no objective can be further improved without hurting the others.

arxiv-2311-04845.title: Bayesian multi-band fitting of alerts for kilonovae detection
arxiv-2311-04845.creator: Biswajit Biswas, Junpeng Lao, Eric Aubourg, Alexandre Boucaud, Axel Guinot, Emille E. O. Ishida, Cécile Roucelle
arxiv-2311-04845.description: Abstract In the era of multi-messenger astronomy, early classification of photometric alerts from wide-field and high-cadence surveys is a necessity to trigger spectroscopic follow-ups. These classifications are expected to play a key role in identifying potential candidates that might have a corresponding gravitational wave (GW) signature.

arxiv-2408-04123.title: Knowledge-based Emotion Recognition using Large Language Models
arxiv-2408-04123.creator: Bin Han, Cleo Yau, Su Lei, Jonathan Gratch
arxiv-2408-04123.description: Abstract Emotion recognition in social situations is a complex task that requires integrating information from both facial expressions and the situational context. While traditional approaches to automatic emotion recognition have focused on decontextualized signals, recent research emphasizes the importance of context in shaping emotion perceptions.

arxiv-2410-22344.title: On merge trees with a given homological sequence
arxiv-2410-22344.creator: Nicholas A. Scoville and Dylan Wen
arxiv-2410-22344.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study the induced homological sequence and the induced merge tree of a discrete Morse function on a tree. A discrete Morse function on a tree gives rise to a sequence of Betti numbers that keep track of the number of components at each critical value.

pmc-10713287.title: Comparison of video assisted thoracoscopic surgery and thoracotomy for treatment of pleural infection stage II and III: a literature review
pmc-10713287.creator: Kasper Steen, Josephine Sørensen, Merete Christensen, René Horsleben Petersen, Babu Naidu, Morten Bendixen, Najib M. Rahman, Christian B. Laursen, Thomas Decker Christensen
pmc-10713287.description: Background and ObjectivePleural infection is associated with significant mortality and morbidity worldwide, with a steadily increasing incidence. We sought to investigate whether video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) or thoracotomy provides the best outcomes in the treatment of stage II and III pleural infection as indications remain controversial.Methods Systematic review of relevant articles from the PubMed database.

pmc-11505922.title: Relationship between Choroidal Thickness and Anterior Scleral Thickness in Patients with Keratoconus
pmc-11505922.creator: Neus Burguera-Giménez, Mª Amparo Díez-Ajenjo, Celeste Briceno-Lopez, Noemí Burguera, Mª José Luque-Cobija, Cristina Peris-Martínez, Adriana Elena Bulboaca, Cristina Nicula
pmc-11505922.description: Purpose: To evaluate the relationship between choroidal thickness (CT) and anterior scleral thickness (AST) in patients with subclinical keratoconus (SKC) and established keratoconus (KC). Methods: This single-center prospective case-control study included 97 eyes of 97 patients: 44 KC eyes, 14 SKC eyes, and 39 age- and axial length (AL)-matched healthy eyes.

pmc-11506888.title: Interleukin-1 Beta (IL1B) and Nerve Growth Factor (NGF): Key Players in Rabbit Reproductive Regulation
pmc-11506888.creator: Gabriella Guelfi, Cecilia Dall’Aglio, Antonello Bufalari, Francesca Mercati, Polina Anipchenko, Camilla Capaccia, Paolo Cocci, Francesco Alessandro Palermo, Gabriele Acuti, Alessandro Troisi, Daniele Tomassoni, Cristiano Boiti, Massimo Zerani, Margherita Maranesi
pmc-11506888.description: Several seminal plasma components, besides NGF, are implicated as ovulation-inducing factors in mammals. This study investigated the IL1B and its receptor IL1R1 in the testis (T), male accessory glands, prostate (P) and seminal vesicles (SV), and uterus (U) of adult rabbits using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and quantitative reverse transcription PCR (RT-qPCR).

pmc-12579416.title: Ofloxacin, paracetamol and cefixime induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome - toxic epidermal necrolysis in an adult female patient: a case report
pmc-12579416.creator: Margi R Desai, Harshita Jaiswal, Mrudangsinh M Rathod, Sakshi Vijayvargi
pmc-12579416.description: BackgroundStevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) represent life-threatening mucocutaneous reactions, predominantly triggered by medications. This case report presents a rare instance of SJS-TEN overlap in a young Indian female precipitated by the combined use of fluoroquinolone (ofloxacin), cephalosporin (cefixime), and paracetamol—an uncommon drug triad not widely reported in existing literature.

pmc-12609605.title: Indirect Effects of Body Dissatisfaction in the Association Between Intolerance of Uncertainty and Disordered Eating Attitudes: A Cross-Sectional Study on Italian University Female Students
pmc-12609605.creator: Giorgia Varallo, Angela Ciaramidaro, Valentina Baldini, Sandro Rubichi, Maristella Scorza, Silvia Cimino
pmc-12609605.description: Objectives: Intolerance of uncertainty (IU) is a transdiagnostic factor implicated in emotional disorders and has recently been linked to maladaptive eating attitudes. Body dissatisfaction, a core risk factor for maladaptive eating, may represent a key pathway through which IU exerts its effects.

pmc-12650328.title: Complementary Yet Distinct Roles of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and SGLT2 Inhibitors in Cardiovascular Risk Reduction
pmc-12650328.creator: Nóra Homoródi, Éva Varga, Zoltán Szabó, Ferenc Sztanek, Mariann Harangi, Marie Černá
pmc-12650328.description: Novel antidiabetic drugs introduced in the last decade have not only revolutionized the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus but have also changed our cardiovascular risk reduction strategy. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists reduce the risk of atherosclerotic diseases primarily through their complex anti-atherosclerotic effect due to their endothelial function-improving, anti-inflammatory, anti-thrombotic, and plaque-stabilizing effects.

pmc-13130087.title: Genome Sequence of the Gordonia rubripertincta Phage Yucky (Cluster CT)
pmc-13130087.creator: Caitlin Carter, Paxton R. Evitts, Cheyenne Helton, Madeline F. Kaiser, Jehee F. Lee, Mackenzie M. Peters, Cade Riley, Mackenzie L. Sanders, Chad Walker, Danielle K. Watt, Pamela L. Connerly, Elizabeth E. Rueschhoff
pmc-13130087.description: Novel bacteriophage Yucky infects Gordonia rubripertincta , a bacterium known for its bioremediation potential. Phage particles have a siphovirus morphology and form 1.2 mm ± 0.5 mm-wide plaques (n=10). The genome of Yucky is 47,803 bp in length and encodes 74 protein-coding genes.
